pebbling_general_foundations.scope: UNBOUNDED theorems: time-reversal symmetry of the reversible pebble game (legal_reverse, exec_reverse_cancel, maxOnes_reverse) and full correctness of Bennett's binary schedule (bennett_general) yielding the achievability half of the reach characterisation: for every p >= 1 a chain of length 2^(p-1) is cleanly reachable with peak p (reach_two_pow). Toward the general impossibility half (Knill Thm 2.3): prefix coverage, roundtrip completeness, and the UNCONDITIONAL restriction lemmas (roadmap step (c)): legality/execution/coverage all commute with restriction to the cells above x (shiftAbove: moves > x re-indexed, x+1 becomes the free left end) and below x (keepBelow), plus the pebble-count split ones = ones(take) + ones(drop). COMPLETED (d)-(f): middle-vertex induction (complete_bound: a complete computation with peak P covers at most 2^P - 1 cells) and the clean-reach corollary (reach_impossible_general: v+1 <= 2^(p-1)). With reach_two_pow this machine-checks the EXACT characterisation reach(p) = 2^(p-1) of Knill 1995 Thm 2.3, both halves fully general

growth_rate_real.scope: UNBOUNDED, but RELATIVE TO submultiplicativity (`Submult`, Lemma 1 of the letter), which is carried as an explicit hypothesis and is not yet formalised in general.  Puts the growth rate c into Lean as a real number: a_k = log f_{k+1} is subadditive, so mathlib's Fekete lemma applies and c := exp(Subadditive.lim).  `growth_le` is the lim = inf phenomenon (c <= f_{m+1}^{1/m} for every finite m); `growth_le_ratio` turns an integer witness f_{m+1} * q^m <= p^m into c <= p/q, which is the form the artifact's witnesses take.  `growth_le_2_6106` instantiates this at m = 59 with RLECertify.fRLE_60 and c_le_2_6106_witness, so the published bound c <= 2.6106 is now a statement about a real number in Lean rather than a step taken on paper.  `growth_le_of_geometric` is the analytic half of the closed-form route: an envelope f_p <= C * B^p gives c <= B, the constant washing out in the Fekete quotient.  Its Nat-side input is supplied in full generality by the stage row_max_closed_form, which assembles c <= 2*sqrt 2.

row_equation_certification.scope: LINK (3), the gap between the general theorems (about `rowIter`) and the machine-checked values (produced by the imperative RLE generator).  Closed by certification rather than by verifying the generator.  (a) UNBOUNDED, kernel axioms only: `mergeFix_unique` -- the self-referential row equation cur = 1 :: smerge prev (cur + prev) has AT MOST ONE solution (entry i depends only on entries < i, so a prefix induction pins the list down; no sortedness, positivity or length hypothesis), hence `eq_rowIter_of_mergeFix`: any list satisfying it IS the generated row.  (b) UNBOUNDED, kernel axioms only: the run-length simulation lemmas `expand_rleMerge` (a whole run may be emitted at once, the only place sortedness is used), `expand_rleZipAdd` and `expand_normRuns`, giving the sound checker `mergeFix_of_checkFix`.  The evaluated definitions are tail-recursive via proved `csimp` lemmas (rows have millions of runs), so no unverified `implemented_by` is involved.  (c) BOUNDED: `chain_sound` + `native_decide` certify the generator's rows level by level, turning them into theorems about `rowIter`; f_10 ... f_60 are now values of `fRow` (S = 50: 1.13 M runs, ~45 s; S = 60: 13.1 M runs, ~9 min, 5.6 GB -- over the usual per-theorem budget on purpose, as the old RLEPebble.rle_f_60 was, because it carries the published bound).  `checkValue` also reads off `fRLE` from the same run, so the generator's own values are DERIVED (`fRLE_10` ... `fRLE_60`) instead of recomputed: the 13.1 M-run row is generated once per build, not twice, and `fRLE_eq_fRow_60` states the bridge explicitly.  `growth_le_2_6106` then puts THE PUBLISHED BOUND on the row-based cost: the numerical upper bound and the structure theorems finally speak about the same object.  The generator itself stays untrusted, as with an unverified solver's checked certificate.

dispersion_on_growth.scope: UNBOUNDED, relative to submultiplicativity.  Connects the dispersion lower bounds to the real number `c` for the first time: they were certified in the language of counts and midpoints (`dispersion_midpoint_16` etc.) and the step 'hence c >= ...' was taken on paper.  `growth_ge_of_midv_geometric` is the general bridge -- a geometric lower bound K*B^S <= m_S on the midpoints becomes (K/2B^2)*(2B)^S <= f_S through Sandwich.two_pow_mul_midv_le_fRow, and GrowthLower.growth_ge_of_geometric reads that as 2B <= c (the side condition K <= B only serves the base level f_1 = 1).  `growth_ge_32_13` applies it to the q = 1 instance: 32/13 = 2.4615... <= c, the first machine-checked improvement over the elementary 2 <= c.  The sharper instances (DispersionBound32*, DispersionBound4731, up to 2.5170647241) fit the same bridge but their midpoint bounds carry fractional exponents (q = 3/2, 47/31) carry fractional exponents, but the CONCLUSION does not: fixing a rational lambda0 below the true ratio turns the whole extraction into Nat arithmetic over one integer comparison (`Dispersion4731Growth.master`, lambda0^47 <= ((2D)/L)^31 cleared of denominators, about 13500 digits, settled by `decide` in a second and depending on NO axiom beyond propext).  `growth_ge_2_51706472` delivers 2.51706472 <= c, within 1.5e-8 of the value the q = 47/31 certificate carries, so the development's sharpest lower bound and its upper bounds now speak about the same real number.  Kernel axioms only.

dispersion_197130.scope: UNBOUNDED, relative to submultiplicativity.  The last affordable member of the dispersion family, and the development's sharpest lower bound on c.  The instance at q delivers c >= 2^{1+V(q)} with V(q) = 1/q - log2 rho_c(q), and kappa* = sup_q V(q) is attained at q* = 1.5153832361...; the deficit falls like (q - q*)^2, so only the convergents of q* are worth instantiating -- 3/2, 47/31, 50/33, 197/130, 8324/5493, ... -- and 197/130 is the last whose constants fit (the next would need L^r with about 7e8 digits against 5e5 here).  `DispersionBound197130` supplies the constants to `DispersionGeneral.dispersion_general`: sigma = rho_c(q)^(1/r) rounded UP to 20 decimals, so rho = sigma^r and lambda = L/D are exactly rational and the rounding is what leaves the slack E = L - D - B >= 1 that absorbs the +1 of the recursion.  `DispersionGeneralGrowth` is `Dispersion4731Growth` with the digits pulled out: from a certificate (D^S(2^S-1))^r <= M^r m_S^n (L^S)^r and a rational lambda0 = P/Q passing the integer master inequality P^n L^r <= Q^n (2D)^r, it delivers 2*(P/Q) <= c, so a new exponent is a new application rather than a new proof script.  With lambda0 = 12585324184468005104/10^19 -- the largest 19-digit rational that passes -- `c_ge_2_5170648368936010208` gives 2.5170648368936010208 <= c, an improvement of 1.1e-8 over the q = 47/31 bound and 2.2e-13 below the conjectured 2^(1+kappa*).  The remaining gap is the deficit of the exponent, not slack in lambda0.  `master` is about 5e5 digits on each side and depends on NO axiom beyond propext; everything else is kernel axioms only, and NO native_decide appears.

dispersion_real_exponent.scope: UNBOUNDED, kernel axioms only, NO CERTIFICATE OF ANY KIND -- the whole DispersionBound* family collapsed into one theorem with real parameters.  `dispersion_real` runs the dispersion induction with the real potential Phi(v) = M * v^q (rpow, not an integer root), so the exponent q, the ratio lam and the split th are ordinary reals subject to the single inequality `hstep`; `midv_pow_lower` specialises it at the midpoints and `root_of_pow_le` takes the q-th root.  `rpow_pow_div` is the one identity the passage needs, (x^n/y)^e = (x^e)^n * y^(-e); `midv_ge_geometric_real` assembles them into the geometric midpoint bound with B = (2/lam)^(1/q) and K = min ((2M)^(-1/q)) B, and `growth_ge_real` feeds that to DispersionGrowth.growth_ge_of_midv_geometric to get 2*(2/lam)^(1/q) <= c.  `c_ge_real` is the same with Submult fRow discharged by BlockSim.submult_fRow, so it is an unconditional statement about the growth rate itself.  WHAT THIS BUYS: the rational instances (dispersion_197130 and the rest) each cost a half-million-digit `decide`, and each is a separate theorem; here lam may be sent down to the critical rho_c(q)^q as a limit in ONE real parameter of ONE theorem.  WHAT REMAINS: Lean has no definition of rho_c yet, so the passage from this family to c >= 2^(1+kappa*) is not in Lean (the enclosure of kappa* lives in the Rocq layer, rocq/KappaStar.v).  The two `example`s in DispersionRealGrowth exercise the chain end to end at (M,q,lam,th) = (2,1,3,1/2) and (4,2,7/4,1/2); the second gives 2.13 <= c from reals alone.  These bounds are not competitive -- they test the passage, not the constant.

critical_root.scope: UNBOUNDED, kernel axioms only, NO CERTIFICATE.  Optimises the real parameter of dispersion_real_exponent.  For fixed theta the two branches of `hstep` force lam >= 1/(1-th^q) (rising in th) and lam >= 1 + (1-th)^q (falling), so the best lam is at the crossing; solving it gives lam* = rho^q and th = 1/(1+rho) where rho is a root of G q rho = rho^(-q) + (1+rho)^(-q) = 1.  `theta_pow` and `one_sub_theta_pow` show BOTH branches then equal rho^q - 1 exactly -- the critical point is where they balance.  WHY A LIMIT: 1/M > 0 for every real M, so `hstep` FAILS at lam = lam*; `c_ge_of_root_gt` proves the bound for every lam > lam* with M = 1 + lam*/(lam-lam*), and `c_ge_of_root` takes the limit along lam = lam* + 1/(n+1) using continuity of lam |-> 2*(2/lam)^(1/q).  This is the limit in ONE real parameter that the certified rational family could not take.  `exists_root` gets the root from the intermediate value theorem on [1, 2^(1/q)+1] (G q 1 = 1 + 2^(-q) > 1 and G q (2^(1/q)+1) < 1/2 + 1/2 = 1; no numerics), and `root_unique` from strict antitonicity of G q, so rho really is rho_c(q).  END PRODUCT `c_ge_critical`: for every q > 0 there is a root rho with 2*2^(1/q)/rho <= c, which is c >= 2^(1+V(q)) for V(q) = 1/q - log2 rho -- written without a logarithm by `bound_eq`.  TEST: at q = 1 the root equation is rho^2 = rho + 1, so rho_c(1) is the golden ratio (`golden_root`) and the bound is the closed form 2*sqrt 5 - 2 = 2.4721... (`c_ge_two_sqrt_five_sub_two`), which beats both the elementary 2 <= c and the first certified bound 32/13 = 2.4615... with no certificate.  WHAT REMAINS: kappa* = sup_q V(q).  Taking that supremum needs the enclosure of the critical q, which is in the Rocq layer (rocq/KappaStar.v) because Lean has no rigorous interval arithmetic; every INDIVIDUAL q is now unconditional inside Lean.

critical_root_rational.scope: BOUNDED (four `decide` certificates per instance), kernel only, no native_decide.  Turns critical_root's conclusion into a DECIMAL.  `c_ge_of_G_le_one` says 2*2^(1/q)/rho <= c whenever G q rho <= 1, but naming a number needs rigorous rational witnesses for 2^(1/q) and rho, which in general means interval arithmetic -- absent from Lean.  IF q = N/R IS RATIONAL there is nothing to enclose: every power becomes an integer comparison (`le_rpow_div`, `rpow_div_le`), so a lower witness a/S for 2^(R/N) is one `decide`, an upper witness u/S for rho_c is three more (bound each summand of G q (u/S), then their sum), and `c_ge_of_certs` packages the four into 2a/u <= c.  Nothing in it is specific to the exponent.  INSTANCES: q = 197/130 gives 2.5170648368936010217 <= c (largest certificate 8826 digits); q = 8324/5493 -- the next convergent of q*, and the SHARPEST LOWER BOUND IN THIS DEVELOPMENT -- gives 2.5170648368938160702 <= c, which is 5.0e-17 below the conjectured 2^(1+kappa*) = 2.5170648368938161206, against 2.2e-13 for 197/130.  COST: certificates are N-th and R-th powers of ~25-digit witnesses, so they grow LINEARLY in N: 8826 digits at 197/130 and 372891 at 8324/5493, and both decide in about 1.0 s (the empty-file baseline).  This is why the convergent after 197/130 is reachable here and was not for dispersion_197130, whose constants are L^r with r the denominator of q -- 5e5 digits already at 197/130 and about 7e8 at the next one.  The 8324/5493 instance needs `exponentiation.threshold` raised (the elaborator declines exponents above 256) and a deeper `maxRecDepth`; that is its whole extra cost.  WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: sup_q V(q) = kappa*.  Pinning one rational q is easy exactly because the expression is not tangent there; at q* it is, so the supremum needs interval arithmetic with Taylor models and stays in rocq/KappaStar.v.

two_d_closed_form.scope: UNBOUNDED, relative to submultiplicativity (as everywhere `c` appears).  **c = 2d**, the letter's closed-form Proposition, as a statement about real numbers: `tendsto_rowMax_root` says the row maxima satisfy M_S^{1/(S-1)} -> c/2, i.e. the limit d exists and c = 2d.  Its only combinatorial input is the sandwich of the stages sandwich_general and row_max_closed_form (2^{S-1} m_S <= f_S <= 2^S M_S and M_S <= S m_S, giving f_S/2^S <= M_S <= S f_S/2^{S-1}); the polynomial factor S washes out under the (S-1)-st root because log S/(S-1) -> 0 (`tendsto_log_div_succ`).  The proof is a squeeze in logarithms around the Fekete convergence `tendsto_logSeq`, which avoids manipulating roots directly.  Kernel axioms only.  This is what makes the row maxima -- the object every structure theorem of this artifact is about -- carry the growth rate itself.

growth_lower_bound.scope: UNBOUNDED, but RELATIVE TO submultiplicativity (as everywhere the real number `c` appears, since `growth` is defined as the Fekete limit).  Fills a structural gap: `GrowthRate` had only upper-bound machinery, so every lower bound in this development (the entropy bound 2.4518, the dispersion family up to 2.5170647) was stated about counts and midpoints and was never a statement about `c` itself.  The asymmetry is real -- the Fekete limit IS an infimum, so one finite value bounds c from above but says nothing from below -- and `growth_ge_of_geometric` supplies the missing direction from an envelope C*B^p <= f_p valid at every level, proved through the convergence `tendsto_logSeq` rather than through lim = inf.  Its input is the general doubling bound `two_mul_fRow_le` (2 f_{S-1} <= f_S, sharper than the bounded-grid PebblingTheory.fval_lower_doubling, which checks f_S >= 2 f_{S-1} - 1 for S <= 7): the merge representation gives row total = 1 + total(prev) + total(B) with B entrywise at least prev, so the total more than doubles at every level, whence 2^{S-1} + 1 <= f_S and `growth_ge_two`: 2 <= c, the growth-rate form of Kralovic's Omega(n log n).  Kernel axioms only.

sandwich_general.scope: UNBOUNDED, kernel axioms only.  The two inequalities of the letter's closed-form Proposition (c = 2d) that were still bounded checks (PebblingTheory.c_eq_2d_sandwich, S <= 8).  `two_pow_mul_midv_le_fRow`: 2^{S-1} m_S <= f_S -- the midpoint sits at index 2^{S-2} - 2 of a row of length 2^{S-1} - 1, so sortedness puts 2^{S-2} + 1 entries at or above m_S.  `rowMax_le_mul_midv`: M_S <= S * m_S -- the maxima telescope into the sum of the midpoint values (rowMax_succ) and the midpoints increase.  The latter needs MIDPOINT MONOTONICITY `midv_le_succ` (m_{S-1} <= m_S), proved here in general from the merge split C_S(v) = 1 + C_{S-1}(v) + #{B <= v} together with B_i >= delta(i,S-1): the count at the new midpoint gives C_{S-1}(m_S) >= 2^{S-2} - 1, which is the position-to-value criterion.  With RowMax.fRow_le_two_pow_mul_rowMax (f_S <= 2^S M_S) the sandwich 2^{S-1} m_S <= f_S <= 2^S M_S <= 2^S S m_S is complete in Lean; the remaining step to c = 2d itself is the real-analytic one (the root limits), which is not formalised.

row_max_closed_form.scope: UNBOUNDED Nat side; the real-number conclusion is RELATIVE TO submultiplicativity (`Submult`, as everywhere in Stage B2).  Closes the closed-form upper bound c <= 2*sqrt 2 of the letter (space-optimal time O(n^{3/2+o(1)}), improving Kralovic's published O(n^{log2 3})).  What was only a bounded check before (PebblingTheory.max_decomposition and the right half of c_eq_2d_sandwich, both S <= 8) is now general: `rowMax_succ` proves the Merge-Lemma max decomposition M_S = m_S + M_{S-1} (the maximum of the convolution term B_i = delta(i,S) + delta(i,S-1) is its last entry, and the previous row ends exactly at the index where the new row's midpoint sits), so the maxima telescope into the sum of the midpoint values.  Fed with the already-general midpoint bound m_S <= 2^{(S-2)/2} (CountRecursion.midpoint_bound_general) this gives `rowMax_envelope`, whose right-hand side is the exact value of sum_j 2^{floor(j/2)}; `fRow_le_two_pow_mul_rowMax` is the trivial f_S <= 2^S M_S (sum <= length * max), and `fRow_envelope` combines them into a geometric envelope of ratio 2*sqrt 2.  `growth_le_two_sqrt_two` runs it through GrowthRate.growth_le_of_geometric.  Unlike growth_le_2_6106 this consumes no computed value: kernel axioms only, no native_decide.  The cost function here is `fRow`, read off the generated row `rowIter`, so this bound lives on the same side of the artifact as the general structure theorems (fRLE, which carries the machine-checked f_60, is still unlinked).

knill_observations_general.scope: UNBOUNDED, kernel axioms only.  Knill 1995's Observation 2.2 and the corner recurrence, which PebblingTheory can only check on bounded grids because its `F` is a lookup into a fixed 64 x 24 table.  On the general row they are theorems: `Fpre_linear` -- Obs 2.2(i), F(n,S) = 2n - 1 for n <= S, STRICTLY STRONGER than the bounded check, which only covers the diagonal S = n; `Fpre_antitone_space` -- Obs 2.2(ii), F is nonincreasing in the space (from the pointwise domination gen_pointwise_dom, valid up to the smaller space's reach limit); `midv_succ_le_two_mul` -- the right half of the midpoint sandwich m_S <= 2 m_{S-1} (the left half is Sandwich.midv_le_succ), from the lower counting recursion seeing the previous row at both v and v/2; and `fRow_corner_recurrence` -- f_S = F(2^{S-2},S) + 2 f_{S-1} at the reach limit, where the split is forced not by finiteness but by LENGTH: with n = 2|prev| + 2 and both parts bounded by |prev| the midpoint is the only feasible cut.

game_cost_achievability.scope: UNBOUNDED, kernel axioms only.  LINK (1) in numerical form: the cost the artifact computes from `rowIter` is achieved by an actual play.  `reachIn_Fpre` runs Knill's construction (game_reach_composition) along the recursion -- the attaining split of `gen_satisfies_knill` supplies the three sub-plays, one at the same space level on a shorter chain and two at one pebble less -- and concludes that for every space level S = s+2 and every chain length n up to the reach limit 2^{S-1} there is a legal play of length exactly Fpre (rowIter s) n.  `GameCost.gameF n S = sInf {t | ReachIn n S t}` makes the game optimum a total function and `gameF_le_fRow` reads the above as gameF (2^{S-1}) S <= f_S.  The converse (no play is shorter) is the remaining half of link (1); with it gameF and fRow coincide and the letter's `Submult` becomes provable by block simulation.  `GameEnvelope.gameF_envelope` spends the achievability immediately: composed with RowMax.fRow_envelope it bounds the GAME's own optimum by 2^{S+1}*2^{floor(S/2)} <= 4*sqrt(2)*n^{3/2} at n = 2^{S-1} -- an inequality between two concrete naturals, so unlike every statement about the real number c it needs neither `Submult` nor `GameOptimal`.  `CutAccounting` supplies the time side of the missing half: `keepBelow`/`shiftAbove` filter on complementary predicates and the re-indexing is a `map`, so a cut at a cell and a time partitions a play's moves exactly (`length_cut`, `length_cut3`) -- Knill's T(S) = T(S1)+T(S2)+T(S3), which the paper writes as obvious.  `ReachLimit` adds the reach characterisation as an iff in the game's own language ((exists t, ReachIn n S t) <-> n <= 2^{S-1}, from reach_two_pow / reach_impossible_general / reachIn_Fpre) and with it the CORNER FORCING in general (`corner_split_forced`, checked on 3 <= p <= 7 in PebblingTheory): at the reach limit both children are playable only for the midpoint split, so the recursion has no choice of cut there.

game_reach_composition.scope: UNBOUNDED, kernel axioms only.  LINK (1), the constructive half.  Introduces the game-side cost as an object: `ReachIn n p t` says the chain of n cells can be cleanly pebbled (empty board to a single pebble on the last cell) with peak <= p in <= t moves by a schedule that stays inside the chain.  The bounded moves are part of the definition on purpose: they make a schedule transportable between boards of different widths, which is the content of the padding lemmas `execB_pad`, `legalB_pad`, `maxOnes_pad` (a play does not notice cells beyond its reach; the peak grows only by the padding's own pebbles).  With those and the four lifting laws of lift_above_primitive, `reach_compose` proves KNILL 1995 Thm 2.1's `<=` half at the level of plays: reach cell m-1 with S, stand on it and reach the far end with S-1 by a LIFTED play, then remove the foundation by running a play that reaches m with S-1 BACKWARDS (legal_reverse / exec_reverse_cancel / maxOnes_reverse).  The peak never exceeds S because each later phase carries exactly one pebble from another phase.  In cost terms this is F(n,S) <= F(m,S) + F(n-m,S-1) + F(m,S-1), the recursion whose solution knill_recursion_uniqueness identifies with `rowIter`.  What remains of link (1) is the `>=` half (the decomposition of an optimal solution matrix, the heavy direction) and the definition of the game optimum as a minimum over plays.

lift_above_primitive.scope: UNBOUNDED, route beta (game-side).  Knill's Thm 2.1 has an asymmetric proof: the `<=` half (LAUR-95-2258 p.5) is a construction composing S1 (reach m with S), S3 (reach n-m from m with S-1) and reversed S2 (unreach m with S-1); the `>=` half decomposes an optimal solution matrix.  The construction needs a play on a short chain LIFTED onto the segment above an already-pebbled foundation.  PebblingFoundations has only the projection shiftAbove; this file supplies the lift and its execution law (above the cut a lifted play does what the original does) and foundation law (below the cut nothing changes, so the foundation survives).  The legality and peak laws are proved too, so all four laws of the lift are available (execution, foundation, legality, peak).  The peak law maxOnes b (lift base s) <= ones (b.take base) + maxOnes (b.drop base) s is the accounting behind "the base is shared", i.e. behind the p + q - 1 of submultiplicativity.  Kernel axioms only.  Still missing for Knill Thm 2.1: a game-level F as a minimum over plays, and the composition theorem assembled from these laws; the >= half of Thm 2.1 (decomposition of an optimal solution matrix) is untouched.

knill_recursion_uniqueness.scope: UNBOUNDED: Knill's recursion has a unique solution.  The structure theorems of this artifact are statements about the generator `gen`/`rowIter`; the bridge to the pebble game has two links, (1) game -> recursion (Knill 1995 Thm 2.1, checked here only on a grid by knill_recursion_agrees_with_game / knillA_agrees_with_F, where `F` is a lookup into a fixed 64x24 table and hence bounded by construction) and (2) recursion -> generator.  Link (2) is proved here in FULL GENERALITY: `solves_unique` shows any two solutions agree on the whole reach range (strong induction on n; a split n = k+l+2 refers back only to l+1 <= n-1), and `solves_eq_gen` identifies every solution with the generated row.  Kernel axioms only, no native_decide.

difference_merge_property_general_core.scope: FULL GENERAL difference-merge property: exchange principle for sorted streams (merged prefix sums = min-split DP value, both directions), multiset preservation, sortedness, PLUS the self-referential closure: generator gen with accumulator-resolved B-stream, invariant (sortedness/bounds), count identity, representation form gen_merge_rep (row = 1 :: smerge prev B) and Knill identity form gen_satisfies_knill for every sorted positive input row.

rle_pebble_values.scope: run-length (RLE) row generator formalised; agreement with the Array DP on S <= 8; exact space-optimal costs f_S for S <= 7 (rle_f_small).  The large values f_10 ... f_60 are no longer computed here: they are certified against `rowIter` in the stage row_equation_certification, which reads BOTH cost functions off the same generator run, so the 13.1 M-run row 60 is generated once per build instead of twice. Read a chain of N*L cells as N blocks of L: every move of an outer play on super-cell i becomes a whole inner play, lifted to block i - forwards to build the block, backwards to clear it (dirPlay, expand). With N = 2^(p-1) and L = 2^(q-1) this is a play on 2^(p+q-2) cells - the reach limit for p+q-1 pebbles - of length f_p * f_q, and RowExact.gameF_eq_fRow_all turns it into Submult fRow. half_reach_optimum_and_recurrence.scope: UNBOUNDED (this work): the half-reach optimum H, the exact min-plus recurrence it satisfies, and the bridge to complete computations. HalfIn is ReachIn with the clean-up dropped - the far end is pebbled at some point and nothing is asked of the final board - and gameH is its optimum. gameT_eq_two_mul_gameH proves T(n,p) = 2 H(n,p) EXACTLY: gameT_le_two_mul_gameH appends the reverse of an optimal half-reach (completeInAt_of_halfIn, via halfIn_tight, which trims a half-reach so that it ENDS with the far end pebbled), and two_mul_gameH_le_gameT cuts an optimal complete computation at a time when the far end is pebbled and reads both pieces as half-reaches, the second played backwards. HalfReachRecurrence restates the predicate as HalfReachIn (with the boundary value H(0,S)=0) and proves BOTH directions of H(n,S) = min_m (F(m,S) + H(n-m,S-1)): halfReach_compose glues a clean checkpoint to a shifted smaller half-reach, halfReach_decompose cuts an arbitrary half-reach at the maximum, over its trace, of the leftmost pebbled cell (the lower prefix is a clean reach, the upper restriction a half-reach with one fewer pebble, and their move sets are disjoint), and halfReach_iff_decomposition packages the two. HalfReachBridge redoes the easy direction for HalfReachIn with no bounded search. gameF_succ_add_one_le_gameT records the direction the manuscript calls non-transferring: F(n,p+1) + 1 <= T(n,p). Every theorem here is in the import cone of RateTransferLow.tendsto_log_gameT_Smin, so the axiom verdict already reached them transitively; listing them makes that coverage visible by name. NOT done here: nothing in this stage identifies the marginal cost stream of H with the merged streams of the F(., i) - that is half_reach_marginal_merge, which is NOT used by any proof.

half_reach_marginal_merge.scope: UNBOUNDED but DISCONNECTED (recorded 2026-09-03). This stage exists so that the manuscript's step (4) has an audited machine referent, and so that the limits of that referent are on the record. WHAT IS PROVED: two list-theoretic facts about a sorted multiset union. half_marginal_merge_is_min_convolution says the prefix sums of `smerge a b` realise the minimum over all splits (the marginal form of a min-plus convolution), and halfMarginals_countLe gives the exact threshold count countLe (halfMarginals rows) x = predictedCount rows x, i.e. D(x) = (number of rows) + sum over rows of count(. <= floor(x/2)). All four theorems rest on propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound only. WHAT IS NOT PROVED, and this is the point: `rows` here is an ARBITRARY List (List Nat). Nothing connects halfMarginals to the actual row family CountRecursion.rowIter, and nothing connects predictedCount to the cost of a HalfReachIn play; the identification of the marginal stream of H with the merged marginal streams of the F(., i) - the discrete-convex infimal convolution step the manuscript's proof of thm:complete goes through - is NOT formalised. MEASURED, not asserted: HalfReachMerge is imported only by the root aggregator RevPebbling.lean, its three definitions (fullMarginals, halfMarginals, predictedCount) occur in no other source, and the module is NOT in the 99-module import cone of RateTransferLow.tendsto_log_gameT_Smin. The rate transfer reaches the same exponent by a capacity pigeonhole that avoids the identification entirely (rate_transfer_left_endpoint).

rate_transfer_scaffold.scope: UNBOUNDED (this work, 2026-09): the scaffold of the rate transfer for COMPLETE computations, and its right endpoint. gameT_mono_len: a complete computation restricts to any prefix of the chain at no extra cost (completeInAt_of_le_len), so T is nondecreasing in the chain length at a fixed budget and the two ends of a minimal-space interval sandwich every n inside it. Smin n = sInf {p | CompleteIn n p} is the minimal feasible budget and Smin_spec identifies it as the least S with n <= 2^S - 1, so Smin is constant on 2^{S-1} <= n <= 2^S - 1. THE HALF-REACH LIMIT: S pebbles half-reach at most 2^S - 1 cells (le_two_pow_sub_one_of_halfReachIn), one short of twice the clean limit 2^{S-1} - reading the clean limit into the half-reach case would be off by a factor of about two, which halfReachIn_three_two witnesses on the play [0,1,0,2]. THE RIGHT ENDPOINT: at n = 2^S - 1 the reach limits pin the split of the min-plus recurrence (H) to a single point, so both halves close (halfReachIn_full, sumF_le_of_halfReachIn) and H(2^S - 1, S) = sum_{i=1}^{S} f_i (gameH_full); time reversal then gives T(2^S - 1, S) = 2 sum_{i<=S} f_i (gameT_full). halfReachIn_iff_halfIn / gameH_bridge_eq identify the two half-reach predicates of the development (far end pebbled AT THE END versus AT SOME TIME) on nonempty chains. This stage does NOT prove the transfer: the growth at the LEFT endpoint n = 2^{S-1}, where the split is not pinned, is rate_transfer_left_endpoint.

rate_transfer_left_endpoint.scope: UNBOUNDED (this work, 2026-09-03): the transfer of the exponential rate to COMPLETE computations at the minimal budget, T(n, S_min(n)) = n^{log2 c + o(1)}, as a Tendsto statement about Real.log (gameT n (Smin n)) / Real.log n (tendsto_log_gameT_Smin). RateTransfer supplied the sandwich (gameT_mono_len) and the right endpoint (gameT_full: T(2^S - 1, S) = 2 sum_{i<=S} f_i); what was missing was the LOWER bound at the left endpoint n = 2^{S-1}, where the split of the min-plus recurrence (H) is not pinned to a single point. It is obtained by a CAPACITY PIGEONHOLE: unrolling (H) writes a half-reach as clean checkpoints m_S, ..., m_1 with m_i <= 2^{i-1}, so if every checkpoint were at most K the chain could only be cap S K = sum_i min(2^{i-1}, K) long; at K = 2^r, S = r+3, n = 2^{r+2} the capacity is 2^{r+2} - 1, exactly one short of the chain, so some checkpoint exceeds K and by itself costs F(K+1, .) (fpre_le_of_halfReachIn, fpre_le_gameH_left). Only the TOP row survives, and its prefix cost is bounded below by the threshold count (fpre_ge_of_countLe: F(k+1,S) >= 2 (k - C_S(v))(v+1)), so DispersionReal.dispersion_real applies unchanged and gives a geometric lower bound with the SAME base 2 (2/lam)^{1/q} that DispersionRealGrowth.c_ge_real gives to f_S itself (gameH_left_ge); the supremum of those bases is c by Final.c_eq_two_rpow_kappaStar (exists_admissible_gt). The upper half needs the right endpoint to collapse to f_S, which is sumF_le_two_mul (sum_{i<=S} f_i <= 2 f_S) from the fact that the row sum at least doubles at every level (rowIter_sum_double: 2 sum(row_s) + 1 <= sum(row_{s+1})). NOT done: the manuscript's own route through the marginal merge is NOT taken here - HalfReachMerge.halfMarginals is still not connected to the actual row family, i.e. the identification of the marginal stream of H with the sorted multiset union of the marginal streams of F(., i) (the discrete-convex infimal convolution) is not formalised. That route is sound and in fact gives a better constant (measured outside Lean: about 0.45 H(2^{S-1},S) against 0.20 here); the pigeonhole merely avoids having to formalise the identification. NOT done either: an effective version with an explicit error term - the o(1) is a Tendsto, and the passage to the supremum over the admissible parameters is non-constructive.

Witness at S = 5: dCount_five_one (decide) gives gameH_sixteen_five_ge, 22 <= H(16,5) (true value 29), against pigeonhole_five = 9 (decide) for the older route.  The exponential rate is the same as RateTransferLow.gameH_left_ge; what this route buys is the constant (measured outside Lean: 0.554 against 0.216 of the true value). erasure_pebbling_model.scope: UNBOUNDED: the erasure game on top of PebblingFoundations (okE / isErase / legalE / erasures; IsPlay = clean plan with peak p and at most e irreversible removals; Reachable, ReachIs, MstarLe, MstarIs, estar). Segment laws for legalE and erasures, and the two bridges to the reversible game: a legalB play is a legalE play with zero erasures, and a legalE play with zero erasures is legalB.

erasure_pebbling_saturation.scope: UNBOUNDED, RC-02 Theorem A (saturation) for p >= 2, n >= 1: M*(n,p,e) = 2n-1 iff e >= e*(n,p) = ceil((n-1)/(p-1)) - 1 (theoremA). Upper bound by the block-sweep construction (theoremA_upper: a clean plan with exactly 2n-1 moves and e*(n,p) erasures); floor 2n-1 for every clean plan (floor_length, Knill Obs. 2.2(i)); lower bound (theoremA_lower, estar_le_erasures) by a state potential pot = ceil((n-1-fb)/(p-1)) + dCount - 1 that is invariant under placements (pot_place) and drops by at most the erasure indicator under removals (pot_remove) along tight plays (tight_of_length: a 2n-1-move plan toggles every cell exactly the forced number of times), replacing the paper's ascent count of the removal permutation. Corollary floor_not_attained: e < e*(n,p) forces M* > 2n-1.

erasure_pebbling_reach.scope: UNBOUNDED, RC-02 Theorem B1: reach(p,e) >= (e+2)*2^(p-2) for p >= 2 (theoremB1), by Bennett's schedule to 2^(p-1) (bennett_seg, via bennett_general) followed by e phases that climb 2^(p-2) cells above a stone and erase the stone (phase_seg). Conjecture B2 at e = 0 in full generality, reach(p,0) = 2^(p-1) (reachIs_zero, via reach_impossible_general). The upper bound of B2 for e >= 1 is the stage erasure_pebbling_b2_upper (2026-11-10).

erasure_pebbling_b2_upper.scope: UNBOUNDED (2026-11-10): Conjecture B2 is a theorem for every p >= 2 and every e, in the ReachIs form (r is reachable AND every reachable n is <= r), r = (e+2)*2^(p-2) (Compression.conjB2 = theoremB1 + Compression.reach_le). The upper bound tracks the number of cells that must be squeezed (width 1 -> 0) to make the board flat for the weighted gap potential wphi: placements and reversible removals keep a flat board flat (wphi_toggle_le_of_place, wphi_zero_of_free), an erasure raises wphi to at most 2^(p-2) (wphi_toggle_le_of_remove), potential k is flattened by squeezing <= k cells (compress), and the target is flat only if the remaining width is <= 2^(p-1) (wphi_target). Does not use RemovalLemma (see erasure_pebbling_removal_reduction).

erasure_pebbling_additive_upper.scope: UNBOUNDED (2026-11-11): the upper half of the additive identity at the maximal reach, M*((e+2)*2^(p-2),p,e) <= M*(2^(p-1),p,0) + e*(M*(2^(p-2),p-1,0)+1) for p >= 2 (mstar_reach_le): the Theorem B1 construction with arbitrary clean sub-plans in place of Bennett's, via extend_right (a play runs unchanged on a board extended to the right) and embed (a clean play lifted onto an empty window above a pebble places exactly the top cell). anchor_6_3_1 instantiates it with two concrete plans checked by decide (M*(6,3,1) <= 13, the tabulated value). The reverse inequality is NOT proved; equality is observed for p <= 6, e <= 6 in data/erasure/.

erasure_pebbling_checker.scope: UNBOUNDED (2026-11-12): a layered search on the boards of IsPlay (lists of Bool), proved to contain every state reachable by an admissible play within peak p and budget e (mem_layer_of_play). Hence an empty layer m refutes MstarLe n p e m (not_mstarLe_of_layer), and with one play of length m it gives MstarIs (mstarIs_of). This is the bridge the bit-mask oracle mstarE lacks; the oracle itself is still unlinked.

erasure_pebbling_counterexample_verified.scope: BOUNDED, native_decide (two layer evaluations), but a statement about IsPlay, not about the oracle (2026-11-12): M*(10,3,3) = 21 and M*(10,4,2) = 19 as MstarIs (counterexample_verified), so the inequality M*(n,p,e+1) <= M*(n,p+1,e) fails at (10,3,2). The upper ends are explicit plays checked by decide (play_10_3_3, play_10_4_2); the lower ends are empty layers (layer_10_3_3, layer_10_4_2) fed to Checker.mstarIs_of. layer_10_4_2_hit is the control that the search does reach the target at the optimum.

erasure_pebbling_removal_reduction.scope: UNBOUNDED but CONDITIONAL and superseded for B2 (2026-11-10). The earlier route to the B2 upper bound through the gap potential phi: B2 follows from RemovalLemma p (conjB2_of_removalLemma), RemovalLemma from FreeRemoval or SlackRemoval, and FreeRemoval from BoundaryStep p (conjB2_of_boundaryStep). RemovalLemma / FreeRemoval / SlackRemoval / BoundaryStep are NOT proved: the theorems taking them as arguments are reductions, not results. Proved unconditionally: phi under placements and erasures (phi_toggle_le_of_place / _of_remove), the target bound (phi_target), the two special removal cases (phi_toggle_le_of_top, phi_toggle_le_of_lowest_free) and sliding (phi_moveUp_le). B2 itself is proved without this route, in erasure_pebbling_b2_upper.

erasure_pebbling_corollaries.scope: UNBOUNDED corollary of Theorem A: the first chain length at which one more erasure lowers the optimal move count is n = (p-1)(e+1)+2 (drop_threshold; estar_threshold computes e* at (p-1)(e+1)+1 and (p-1)(e+1)+2), matching data/erasure/drops.md.

erasure_pebbling_first_drop.scope: UNBOUNDED (2026-11-17): the first drop is exactly two moves. For every p >= 3 and e, at n = (p-1)(e+1)+2: M*(n,p,e) = 2n+1 and M*(n,p,e+1) = 2n-1 (first_drop). Lower end: drop_threshold (floor not attained) plus the parity law that every clean plan has odd length (length_odd). Upper end: an explicit plan (drop_construction): an opening of 2p+3 moves that holds cell 1 as a stepping stone (opening_spec), then sweep_spec. Corollaries close the whole table for p = 3 (mstar_p3_floor, mstar_p3_drop, unreachable_p3) and for p = 2 (mstar_p2). Lifts the 2026-11-11 paper proofs to layer 1; mutation test 3/3 detected, control passes.

erasure_pebbling_contraction.scope: UNBOUNDED (2026-11-17): contraction lower bound. For every p >= 2, n >= 1 and every clean plan s with peak p and at most e erasures, with A = (p-1)(e+1)+1: 4n <= |s| + 1 + 2A (contraction_bound), i.e. |s| >= 2n-1 + 2*max(0, n-A) (length_ge). A plan longer than 2n-1 re-places some cell; the lowest such cell is contracted (contract_drop for cell 0, contract_merge = OR-merge with the cell below otherwise) into a clean plan on n-1 cells with no larger peak, no more erasures and at least 4 fewer moves; the tight case is theoremA_lower. Corollaries: near_band_lower (n = A+j gives >= 2n-1+2j), p4_lower (n >= 3e+4 gives >= 4n-6e-9), first_drop_tight (j = 1 is attained). Only lower bounds here; the matching upper constructions (n <= T(p)+e*T(p-1)) are erasure_pebbling_triangular. Lifts the 2026-11-11 paper proof to layer 1; mutation test 4/4 detected, control passes.

erasure_pebbling_triangular.scope: UNBOUNDED (2026-11-17): the contraction bound is attained up to the triangular frontier. With T(p) = p(p-1)/2+1 (tri, tri_eq) and A = (p-1)(e+1)+1: for every p >= 3, e >= 0 and 1 <= n <= T(p) + e*T(p-1), M*(n,p,e) = 2n-1 + 2*max(0, n-A) (mstar_exact). Upper side: tri_spec (p >= 2, p <= n <= T(p): peak p, no erasure, 4n-2p-1 moves, by splitting n = a+b and running the (p-1)-plan above a held stone) and blocks_spec (e blocks of length in [p-1, T(p-1)], one erasure each), built from window_seg (a play shifted into a window above a held stone) and Seg.reverse. Lower side: Contraction.length_ge. Corollaries: near_band_exact (n = A+j, j <= p-2), mstar_p4_interior (M*(n,4,e) = 4n-6e-9 for 3e+4 <= n <= 4e+7), mstar_p5_interior (M*(n,5,e) = 4n-8e-11 for 4e+5 <= n <= 7e+11). Not covered: n > T(p)+e*T(p-1) (see erasure_pebbling_next_point for n = T(p)+e*T(p-1)+1) and the structural statement that optimal plans use exactly e erasures. Lifts the 2026-11-11 paper proof to layer 1; mutation test 6/6 detected, control passes.

erasure_pebbling_next_point.scope: UNBOUNDED (2026-11-17): one past the triangular frontier. For every p >= 4, e >= 0 and n = T(p) + e*T(p-1) + 1, with L0 = 2n-1 + 2(n-A): a clean plan with L0+2 moves exists (next_spec: the 25-move seed seed_p4 for p = 4, checked by decide, lifted to larger p by lift, then e erasure blocks), and every plan has length L0 or >= L0+2 (next_point, from Contraction.length_ge and length_odd). For p = 4, n = 4e+8: 23+10e <= M* <= 25+10e (p4_endpoint). Whether L0 is attained is NOT decided; numerically the priced recurrence of Thumann-Soloveichik excludes it (scripts/erasure_ts_lagrangian.py, layer 2). Lifts the upper bound of the 2026-11-11 paper note; mutation test 5/5 detected, control passes.

erasure_pebbling_bounded.scope: BOUNDED, native_decide, ORACLE LEVEL: the bit-mask BFS oracle mstarE / reachableE of ErasurePebbling/Basic.lean (same rules as IsPlay, not linked to it by proof) reproduces the RC-02 anchors M*(4,3,.)=9,7,7,7; M*(6,4,.)=15,11,11,11; M*(16,5,.)=71,45,37,31; M*(16,6,0)=51; M*(16,7,0)=49; M*(16,6,1)=41; M*(17,6,0)=57 (anchors_table); at r = (e+2)*2^(p-2) the oracle reaches r and does not reach r+1 for p=3 (e<=6), p=4 (e<=4), p=5 (e<=2) (conjB2_p3/p4/p5; weaker than ReachIs, which quantifies over every n > r; the general ReachIs form is Compression.conjB2); the inequality M*(n,p,e+1) <= M*(n,p+1,e) for n <= 2^(p-1), p<=4, e<=3 (ineq_small) and its counterexample M*(10,3,3)=21 > 19=M*(10,4,2) (ineq_counterexample; the same two values as statements about IsPlay are Checker.counterexample_verified); non-monotonicity M*(16,5,0)=71 > 57=M*(17,6,0) (non_monotone_16_17).
